summary: Nearly 400 AI experts and leaders, including Sam Altman and executives from Google and Microsoft, signed a statement warning that mitigating the risk of extinction from AI should be a global priority alongside pandemics and nuclear war. The statement, posted by the Center for AI Safety, sparked pushback from critics who see it as overhyped and distracting from more immediate AI harms like disinformation. The article cites prior calls for a pause, Altman's EU threat, and recent incidents like a fake Pentagon image that briefly moved markets.

claims.text: A statement warning that AI could lead to human extinction was published Tuesday by the Center for AI Safety, a San Francisco-based nonprofit.
claims.evidence_quote: The statement was posted to the website of the Center for AI Safety, a San Francisco-based nonprofit organization.

claims.text: The full statement says: 'Mitigating the risk of extinction from AI should be a global priority alongside other societal-scale risks such as pandemics and nuclear war.'
claims.evidence_quote: Mitigating the risk of extinction from AI should be a global priority alongside other societal-scale risks such as pandemics and nuclear war.

claims.text: The statement was signed by almost 400 people, including Sam Altman, top AI executives from Google and Microsoft, and 200 academics.
claims.evidence_quote: It’s signed by almost 400 people, including some of the biggest names in the field — Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT, as well as top AI executives from Google and Microsoft and 200 academics.

claims.text: Meredith Whittaker, president of Signal and chief adviser to the AI Now Institute, mocked the statement as tech leaders overpromising their product.
claims.evidence_quote: Meredith Whittaker, president of the encrypted messaging app Signal and chief adviser to the AI Now Institute, a nonprofit group devoted to ethical AI practices, mocked the statement as tech leaders overpromising their product.

claims.text: Clément Delangue, CEO of Hugging Face, tweeted an edited version of the statement that substituted 'AGI' for 'AI.'
claims.evidence_quote: Clément Delangue, co-founder and CEO of the AI company Hugging Face, tweeted a picture of an edited version of the statement subbing in "AGI" for AI.

claims.text: AGI, or artificial general intelligence, is a theoretical form of AI that is as capable or more capable than humans.
claims.evidence_quote: AGI stands for artificial general intelligence, which is a theoretical form of AI that is as capable or more capable than humans.

claims.text: Two months earlier, Elon Musk, Steve Wozniak, and Grady Booch signed a petition calling for a pause on large-scale AI research; none of them signed the new statement.
claims.evidence_quote: The statement comes two months after a different group of AI and tech leaders, including Tesla owner Elon Musk, Apple co-founder Steve Wozniak, and IBM chief scientist Grady Booch, signed a petition calling for a “pause“ on all large-scale AI research that was open to the public. None of them have yet signed the new statement, and such a pause has not happened.

claims.text: Sam Altman held a private dinner with dozens of House members and had an amicable Senate hearing, becoming a rare tech executive whom both parties warmed to.
claims.evidence_quote: He held a private dinner with dozens of House members and was the subject of an amicable Senate hearing, where he became the rare tech executive whom both parties warmed to.

claims.text: Altman said last week that OpenAI could leave the European Union if AI became 'overregulated.'
claims.evidence_quote: Last week, he said that OpenAI could leave the European Union if AI became "overregulated."

claims.text: There is no indication that the United States has imminent plans for large-scale regulation of the AI industry.
claims.evidence_quote: There is no indication that the United States has imminent plans for large-scale regulation of the industry.

claims.text: Gary Marcus said: 'Literal extinction is just one possible risk, not yet well-understood, and there are many other risks from AI that also deserve attention.'
claims.evidence_quote: Literal extinction is just one possible risk, not yet well-understood, and there are many other risks from AI that also deserve attention.

claims.text: Microsoft President Brad Smith said that deepfakes and their potential use for disinformation are his biggest worries about AI.
claims.evidence_quote: Microsoft President Brad Smith has said that deepfakes and the potential that they would be used for disinformation are his biggest worries about the technology.

claims.text: Last week, markets briefly dipped after a fake, seemingly AI-generated image of an explosion near the Pentagon went viral on Twitter.
claims.evidence_quote: Last week, markets briefly dipped after a fake, seemingly AI-generated image of an explosion near the Pentagon went viral on Twitter.
